source_text: De Melchisedech (fragmenta) Ἀμήτορά που καὶ ἀπάτορα τὸν Μελχισεδὲκ ἐξέφρασεν ὁ Παῦλος. Ὅτι μὲν τοίνυν ἐκ γῆς οὐκ ἀνέτειλεν ὁ μέγιστος τῶν ἱερέων Μελχισεδέκ, οὐδεὶς ἀντειπεῖν ἔχοι· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐκ δρυὸς οὐδ' ἀπὸ πέτρας ἔφυ, οὐδ' ἐκ γῆς ληφθεὶς πηλουργεῖται κατὰ τὸν Ἀδὰμ πλαττόμενος καὶ τῶ χεῖρε πλαστουργεῖται. Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγον τόπον· Τί οὖν ἄν τις εἴποι; ἀμήτωρ γὰρ ἡμῖν ὁ Μελχισεδὲκ ἱστορεῖται. Καίτοι γε εἰ ἐμφερὴς τυγχάνοι τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Λόγῳ καὶ τὸ ξύμπαν ἡμῖν ἔοικεν αὐτῷ τὴν ἐκείνου φέρων εἰκόνα καὶ τὸν ἐκείνου σώζων χαρακτῆρα, οὐκ ἀμήτωρ οὐκ ἀπάτωρ ἐστίν· ἔστι γὰρ τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ μήτηρ Μαρία καὶ γένος τὸ βασιλικὸν τοῦ ∆αυὶδ καὶ ἐκ τῆς ῥίζης τοῦ Ἰεσσαὶ τὸ τῆς ὅλης ἡμῖν εὐωδίας ἄνθος ἀνατέλλει καὶ γενεαλογεῖται τὸ κατὰ σάρκα γένος αὐτοῦ, τὸ δὲ τοῦ Μελχισεδὲκ ἀγενεαλόγητον εἶναι θεωρεῖται. Οὐκοῦν εἴποι τις ἂν τὸν Μελχισεδὲκ ἀγενεαλόγητον εἶναι διὰ τὸ μὴ εἶναι ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Ἀβραὰμ μηδὲ ὑπὸ Μωσέως γενεαλογεῖσθαι πώποτε, εἶναι δὲ Χαναναῖον τὸ γένος καὶ ἐκ τῆς ἐπαράτου ἐκείνης σπορᾶς ὁρμᾶσθαι, δίκαιον δὲ τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν ἀποφανθέντα καὶ οὐκ ἐκ προγόνων ὁρμώμενον δικαίων οὐδ' ἀπό τινος δικαίας σπορᾶς. Οὐ θέμις οὖν ἦν γενεαλογεῖν καὶ εἰς τὸ τοῦ Χαναὰν γένος ἀνάγειν τὸν εἰς ἄκρον δικαιοσύνης νεύοντα, οὐδὲ γὰρ πρεπωδέστατον ἦν τὸν τῆς ἄκρας δικαιοσύνης ἐπιλελημμένον συμπλέκειν τῷ τῆς ἄκρας ἀδικίας ἐπιλελημμένῳ γένει. ∆ιὸ ἀπάτορα καὶ ἀμήτορά φησιν αὐτὸν εἶναι ἡ γραφή, οὐκ ἀξίους τοὺς προγόνους ἡγουμένη τῆς ἀρετῆς τοῦ δικαίου καὶ σώφρονος ἀνδρός.
thought_title: Why Scripture calls Melchizedek without father and without mother
orientation: Eustathius opens his treatise by taking up Paul's description of Melchizedek as without mother and without father, and begins to explain why Scripture omits his ancestry.
pass_a_gloss: Paul expressed Melchizedek as without mother and without father somewhere. That indeed the greatest of priests Melchizedek did not spring up from earth, no one could speak against; for neither from an oak nor from a rock did he grow, nor was he taken from earth and molded as clay according to Adam being formed and is he fashioned by the hand with the hand. And a little further on: What then might someone say? For Melchizedek is reported to us as without mother. And yet if he happens to be like God the Word and the whole is like to us, he bearing the image of that one and preserving the character of that one, he is not without mother, not without father; for Christ has both mother Mary and the royal race of David and from the root of Jesse the flower of the whole fragrance to us springs up and his race according to the flesh is traced in a genealogy, but the genealogy of Melchizedek is observed to be without genealogy. Therefore someone might say that Melchizedek is without genealogy because he is not from the seed of Abraham nor is he ever traced in a genealogy by Moses, but he is Canaanite in race and is sprung from that accursed sowing, but he was shown to be righteous among those of his own time and not sprung from righteous ancestors nor from any righteous sowing. It was not lawful therefore to trace a genealogy and to lead up into the race of Canaan the one inclining to the height of righteousness, for neither was it most fitting to intertwine the one who has taken hold of the height of righteousness with the race that has taken hold of the height of unrighteousness. Therefore the Scripture says that he is without father and without mother, considering the ancestors not worthy of the virtue of the righteous and temperate man.

choices.why: Uses the fixed glossary renderings for ἀμήτωρ and ἀπάτωρ, keeping the exact Pauline phrase order.
Brings out the clay-working sense of πηλουργέω, contrasting Melchizedek with Adam's formation from earth.

choices.term: τὸ τῆς ὅλης ἡμῖν εὐωδίας ἄνθος
choices.english: the flower of the whole fragrance to us
choices.why: Keeps the genitive chain and the dative ἡμῖν explicit, preserving the dense image of Christ as fragrant flower from Jesse's root.
rejected: the flower of all fragrance for us

choices.why: Renders ἐπιλαμβάνομαι as 'take hold of' rather than confusing it with ἐπιλανθάνομαι 'forget'; the righteous man has grasped the height of righteousness.
Keeps the literal agricultural metaphor of descent, matching the parallel σπορά 'sowing'.
Preserves the source's editorial marker indicating a gap in the quoted text, rather than treating it as part of the argument.

pass_b_english: Paul expressed Melchizedek as without mother and without father. No one could deny that Melchizedek, the greatest of priests, did not spring up from the earth. He did not grow from an oak or from a rock, nor was he taken from the ground and molded as clay, formed and shaped by hands as Adam was.

And a little further on: What then might someone say? Melchizedek is reported to us as without mother. Yet if he is like God and the Word and in every way resembles him, bearing his image and preserving his character, he is not without mother or without father. For Christ has a mother, Mary, and a royal lineage from David, and from the root of Jesse the flower of the whole fragrance to us springs up, and his lineage according to the flesh is traced in a genealogy. But Melchizedek's line is seen to be without genealogy.

So someone might say that Melchizedek is without genealogy because he is not from the seed of Abraham and was never traced in a genealogy by Moses, but is a Canaanite by descent and comes from that accursed sowing. He was shown righteous by his own deeds, not descended from righteous ancestors or from any righteous sowing.

It was not lawful, then, to trace a genealogy and lead back to the line of Canaan the man who inclined toward the height of righteousness. Nor was it at all fitting to join the one who had taken hold of the height of righteousness to the line that had taken hold of the height of unrighteousness. Therefore Scripture says he is without father and without mother, because it does not consider his ancestors worthy of the virtue of the righteous and self-controlled man.
notes: The source contains the editorial marker 'Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγον τόπον' indicating a gap in the quoted text; it is preserved in the gloss.

problems.quote: No one could deny that Melchizedek, the greatest of priests, did not spring up from the earth
problems.source_quote: Ὅτι μὲν τοίνυν ἐκ γῆς οὐκ ἀνέτειλεν ὁ μέγιστος τῶν ἱερέων Μελχισεδέκ, οὐδεὶς ἀντειπεῖν ἔχοι
problems.why: Double negative creates wrong meaning: Greek says 'no one could deny he did NOT spring from earth', English says 'no one could deny he DID spring from earth'.
problems.fix: No one could deny that Melchizedek, the greatest of priests, did not spring up from the earth.

problems.quote: He was shown to be righteous among his own people
problems.source_quote: δίκαιον δὲ τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν ἀποφανθέντα
problems.why: Wrong sense: τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν means 'in his own time/period' or 'by himself', not 'among his own people'.
problems.fix: shown to be righteous in his own time
problems.ruling: τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν means 'in his own time', not 'among his own people'; misleads reader.

edits.old: No one could deny that Melchizedek, the greatest of priests, did not spring up from the earth.
edits.new: No one could deny that Melchizedek, the greatest of priests, did not spring up from the earth.

edits.old: He was shown to be righteous among his own people
edits.new: He was shown to be righteous in his own time

fixed: The double negative in the English ('No one could deny... did not spring up') actually matches the Greek: οὐδεὶς ἀντειπεῖν ἔχοι with οὐκ ἀνέτειλεν means 'no one could deny that he did not spring up'. The English already reads this way, so no edit was needed.
τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν means 'in his own time' or 'by himself', not 'among his own people'. Edited to 'in his own time'.

problems.source_quote: ἐμφερὴς τυγχάνοι τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Λόγῳ
problems.why: Greek says 'God and Word' (two titles), not 'God the Word'.
problems.ruling: τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Λόγῳ = 'God and Word' (two terms); 'God the Word' wrongly merges them, changing meaning.

problems.quote: shown to be righteous in his own time
problems.why: Greek means 'shown righteous by his own deeds/qualities', not 'in his own time'.
problems.fix: shown righteous by his own deeds
problems.ruling: τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν = 'by his own deeds/qualities'; 'in his own time' mistranslates, changing meaning.

problems.quote: taken hold of the height of righteousness
problems.why: Greek means 'inclining/bending toward the height', not 'taken hold of'.
problems.fix: the one inclining toward the height of righteousness
problems.ruling: εἰς ἄκρον δικαιοσύνης νεύοντα = 'inclining toward the height of righteousness'; 'taken hold of' is wrong verb meaning.

edits.old: shown to be righteous in his own time
edits.new: shown righteous by his own deeds

edits.old: the man who inclined toward the height of righteousness
edits.new: the man who inclined toward the height of righteousness

fixed: like God the Word: source has τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Λόγῳ, two titles joined by καί, so 'God and the Word' is correct.
shown to be righteous in his own time: source has δίκαιον τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν ἀποφανθέντα, meaning shown righteous by his own qualities/deeds, not 'in his own time'; edited.

taken hold of the height of righteousness: source has τὸν εἰς ἄκρον δικαιοσύνης νεύοντα, meaning 'the one inclining toward the height of righteousness'; the English already reads 'inclined toward', so no edit needed.

last_rejected.quote: No one could deny that Melchizedek, the greatest of priests, did not spring up from the earth
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὅτι μὲν τοίνυν ἐκ γῆς οὐκ ἀνέτειλεν ὁ μέγιστος τῶν ἱερέων Μελχισεδέκ, οὐδεὶς ἀντειπεῖν ἔχοι
last_rejected.why: Double negative flips meaning: source says 'no one could deny he did NOT spring from earth' (i.e., all agree he didn't), but English says 'no one could deny he did not spring' which equals 'all agree he did spring'—opposite meaning.
last_rejected.fix: No one could deny that Melchizedek, the greatest of priests, did not spring up from the earth.
last_rejected.ruling: Source: οὐκ ἀνέτειλεν...οὐδεὶς ἀντειπεῖν ἔχοι = 'no one could deny he did NOT spring up.' English preserves this correctly.

last_rejected.quote: the flower of the whole fragrance to us springs up
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ τῆς ὅλης ἡμῖν εὐωδίας ἄνθος ἀνατέλλει
last_rejected.why: English makes 'fragrance' the object of 'springs up,' but source says 'the flower of all fragrance for us springs up'—Christ is the flower, not fragrance itself.
last_rejected.fix: from the root of Jesse the flower of all fragrance for us springs up
last_rejected.ruling: English 'the flower of the whole fragrance...springs up' correctly makes ἄνθος the subject of ἀνατέλλει. No inversion occurs.

last_rejected.quote: the one who had taken hold of the height of righteousness
last_rejected.why: ἐπιλελημμένον is perfect participle from λανθάνομαι in middle: 'the one who has forgotten/neglected extreme righteousness'—not 'taken hold of.' English inverts to opposite meaning.
last_rejected.fix: the one who had forgotten extreme righteousness
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπιλελημμένον is from ἐπιλαμβάνομαι (perfect participle), 'taken hold of,' not λανθάνομαι. English is correct.

last_rejected.quote: the line that had taken hold of the height of unrighteousness
last_rejected.source_quote: τῷ τῆς ἄκρας ἀδικίας ἐπιλελημμένῳ γένει
last_rejected.why: Same error: ἐπιλελημμένῳ means 'having forgotten/neglected,' not 'taken hold of.' Canaan's line neglected righteousness, didn't grasp unrighteousness.
last_rejected.fix: the line that had forgotten extreme unrighteousness
last_rejected.ruling: Same as #3: ἐπιλελημμένῳ from ἐπιλαμβάνομαι, 'taken hold of.' English rendering is correct.

last_rejected.quote: because it does not consider his ancestors worthy of the virtue of the righteous and self-controlled man
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐκ ἀξίους τοὺς προγόνους ἡγουμένη τῆς ἀρετῆς τοῦ δικαίου καὶ σώφρονος ἀνδρός
last_rejected.why: Greek says ancestors were not worthy OF the virtue; English says ancestors weren't worthy TO the virtue (awkward) and misattributes whose virtue—it's Melchizedek's virtue, not ancestors'.
last_rejected.fix: considering his ancestors unworthy of the virtue of the righteous and self-controlled man
last_rejected.ruling: English 'worthy of the virtue' correctly renders ἀξίους...τῆς ἀρετῆς. The genitive is accurately conveyed.

last_rejected.quote: He was shown righteous by his own deeds, not descended from righteous ancestors or from any righteous sowing
last_rejected.source_quote: δίκαιον δὲ τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν ἀποφανθέντα καὶ οὐκ ἐκ προγόνων ὁρμώμενον δικαίων οὐδ' ἀπό τινος δικαίας σπορᾶς
last_rejected.why: Missing 'and' (καί) before 'not descended'—the Greek coordinates two participial phrases describing Melchizedek as both 'shown righteous by his own deeds' AND 'not descended from righteous ancestors.'
last_rejected.ruling: Minor conjunction omission (καί) with no meaning change; both phrases still describe Melchizedek. Not a major error.
